scope: Documented Codex mode in the current desktop app, plus explicitly separated broader desktop capabilities. Official legacy Codex app links now redirect to ChatGPT desktop documentation. Availability varies by plan, rollout, permissions and OS; no exact installed desktop version is asserted.

statusMeaning.Present: The bounded feature exists in the pushed Station client, not blanket parity for its entire category.
statusMeaning.Partial: Useful foundation exists but named acceptance criteria are incomplete.
statusMeaning.Missing: No shipped Station capability was identified; a related service implementation is reuse potential, not client parity.

findings.feature: Create and resume a coding session
findings.codex: Project chats preserve ongoing work.
findings.station: Can inspect existing SLIPSTREAM workstreams and send a direction; cannot start a general local coding session or bind one to an authorized checkout.
findings.gap: Session creation and a stable mapping among workstream, runtime session, checkout and target.
findings.reuse: SLIPSTREAM workstream/cycle/conversation identities; Station resource references.
findings.acceptance: Start from an authorized repository, close its tab, reopen and recover the same session.

findings.codex: Runtime events support incremental agent and tool output.
findings.station: Conversation is rendered from fetched payloads; no streamed turn/item event consumer or replay cursor.
findings.gap: Typed event stream, reconnection/replay, command and file-change cards, visible run state.
findings.reuse: SLIPSTREAM cycles, prompts, responses and worker events already exist.
findings.acceptance: See a real command start, output and finish without manual Refresh; reconnect without duplicated items.

findings.feature: Steer, queue and stop active work
findings.codex: Running work supports follow-up direction and interruption.
findings.station: Station only submits /agent; audited SLIPSTREAM askAgent rejects another prompt while a reply is in flight. No Station stop/steer transport.
findings.gap: Service-level semantics for steering versus queued follow-up, acknowledged cancellation and child-process cleanup.
findings.reuse: Extend existing workstream/cycle state rather than treating Send direction as a stop/steer operation.
findings.acceptance: Send a correction during an active command; receive an explicit steering receipt; stop and confirm execution actually ends.

findings.feature: Local coding tools and verification loop
findings.codex: Codex can operate in a selected local project.
findings.station: Human terminals run locally, while agent messages go to SLIPSTREAM. No agent tool host can safely read, patch, run and verify an authorized local checkout through Station.
findings.gap: Authorized local worker/runtime integration with durable command and file-change records.
findings.reuse: ConPTY is reusable for human terminals; audit existing SLIPSTREAM worker and sandbox contracts before extending execution.
findings.acceptance: An agent fixes a bounded local bug, runs the relevant check and presents the actual changed files.

findings.codex: Goal mode exposes persistent progress and pause/resume controls.
findings.station: Tasks/statuses are visible, but no plan/goal editor, goal budget or goal lifecycle in Station.
findings.gap: Goal-to-workstream contract, visible completion criteria, explicit pause/resume/blocked states.
findings.reuse: SLIPSTREAM projects, tasks and cycles; CONTINUUM coordination.
findings.acceptance: Define a goal, inspect its plan, pause/resume and recover its state in another client.

findings.codex: Subagent activity and conversations can be inspected.
findings.station: Multiple workstreams can be opened, but there is no parent/child agent view or child steering controls.
findings.gap: Stable delegation relationships, activity aggregation, inherited permissions and conflict-aware execution isolation.
findings.reuse: Audit SLIPSTREAM agent-session and workstream relationships.
findings.acceptance: Run two isolated subtasks, inspect each result and permissions, and return to their parent workstream.

findings.feature: Open and bind a local repository
findings.codex: Local projects attach to folders.
findings.station: Projects are service records; repository URLs are links. No local root picker, clone flow or verified path binding.
findings.gap: Attach a trusted local root to a project/target, distinguish Windows versus WSL paths and persist that association.
findings.reuse: Existing project repository metadata and qualified resource identity.
findings.acceptance: Open a project and identify the exact checkout/branch/root before any local agent operation.

findings.codex: Parallel chats can use isolated Git worktrees and hand work back to Local.
findings.station: No worktree creation, branch selection, cleanup or handoff implementation.
findings.gap: Worktree lifecycle tied to workstreams, dirty-tree protection and explicit merge/handoff recovery.
findings.reuse: Use Git and the existing execution target; do not create a second task database.
findings.acceptance: Run two changes in one repository without collisions and safely hand one back to the main checkout.

findings.codex: Built-in Git controls include a diff pane and inline feedback.
findings.station: No changed-file list, text/code viewer, hunk diff or inline review comments.
findings.gap: Contextual Changes surface with read-only diffs first, then reversible hunk operations and feedback.
findings.reuse: Workstream resources and repository metadata; preserve the decision to avoid a standalone Files app.
findings.acceptance: Select a changed file, inspect its diff, cite a line and request a targeted correction without opening another app.

findings.feature: Stage, commit, push and pull request
findings.codex: Desktop Git actions cover staging/reverting, commits, pushes and PR creation.
findings.station: A user can type Git commands in a terminal; Station has no Git state/actions or remote-provider integration.
findings.gap: Branch/change summary, stage/revert controls, commit and explicit consequential push/PR actions.
findings.reuse: Git CLI/library and existing GitHub/GitLab account contracts.
findings.acceptance: Review, stage and commit selected changes, then explicitly push and open a PR with correct repository context.

findings.codex: Code Review surfaces PR changes, feedback and checks.
findings.station: Repository URLs open as websites; no native PR/MR details, findings, comment resolution or checks.
findings.gap: Reusable review capability with revision-qualified file and comment references.
findings.reuse: Existing source-host integrations in the ecosystem, after contract audit.
findings.acceptance: Open an authorized PR, inspect a finding against the right revision and navigate to its changed file.

findings.codex: Local environments define worktree setup and terminal actions.
findings.station: No project action registry, setup lifecycle, environment selection or run/build shortcuts.
findings.gap: Project-scoped actions with explicit target, working directory, permissions and failure output.
findings.reuse: Existing repository definitions and ARCHER installation/preflight contracts.
findings.acceptance: Run a declared build in the correct checkout; new worktrees receive their required setup.

findings.codex: Agent execution separates enforced sandbox boundaries from approval policy.
findings.station: Remote pages lack the native bridge and service approvals exist, but human ConPTY sessions are not an agent sandbox.
findings.gap: OS-enforced agent filesystem/network/process policy plus scoped command approval and audit records.
findings.reuse: Existing worker isolation and, optionally, an established agent runtime sandbox.
findings.acceptance: A local agent can edit its authorized checkout but a denied outside write/network request remains blocked.

findings.codex: Agent workflows expose explicit approvals.
findings.station: Station has one-use confirmation challenges for SLIPSTREAM task approve/reject, with service authorization.
findings.gap: Generalize presentation to typed command/file/network decisions without weakening existing task approval.
findings.reuse: Existing approval.prepare/commit and service task authorization.
findings.acceptance: A decision shows exact resource, target and consequence, can be denied and cannot be replayed.

findings.feature: Local, worktree and cloud target selection
findings.codex: Codex distinguishes Local, Worktree and Cloud execution.
findings.station: Local human shells and service cycles are distinguished, but Infrastructure has no authorized target selector or resource inventory.
findings.gap: Explicit target capabilities, availability, workload/status and selected execution scope.
findings.reuse: NEBULA/NUCLEUS inventory and SLIPSTREAM execution targets; no inferred remote shell from a URL.
findings.acceptance: Choose a permitted target before running; an unavailable cloud target cannot silently become local execution.

findings.codex: Desktop projects can use SSH hosts; remote clients can reach connected computers.
findings.station: No SSH connection management, host trust/pairing, remote file/command transport or disconnect recovery.
findings.gap: Authenticated host identity, target-specific permissions, connection lifecycle and auditable remote operations.
findings.reuse: Existing machine/fabric contracts in NUCLEUS and network identity in NEBULA.
findings.acceptance: Reconnect to an authorized host and resume the same workstream without copying broad credentials into the shell.

findings.codex: Codex supports ChatGPT/API-key sign-in and model-dependent settings.
findings.station: Station authenticates PARALLAX services, not an AI provider. Model choice is not exposed in Station; SLIPSTREAM already resolves a team model on the server.
findings.gap: Provider/runtime adapter with dedicated supported authentication, model discovery, reasoning settings and provenance.
findings.reuse: SLIPSTREAM AiModelCatalog; never pass NEXUS/device credentials to model providers.
findings.acceptance: Choose an available model/runtime, see which account funds execution and preserve that choice with the session.

findings.codex: Desktop settings provide token activity; model limits/settings vary.
findings.station: No token/context meter, rate-limit state, estimated cost or enforceable workstream budget UI.
findings.gap: Expose measured usage and limits, distinguish estimates from billed data and persist execution budgets.
findings.reuse: Existing cycle/driver identity; audit provider usage and QUARK financial contracts before adding accounting.
findings.acceptance: A run reports measured usage and a budget stop is enforced by execution infrastructure.

findings.codex: Project guidance, memories and skills carry reusable context.
findings.station: Stable service workstreams exist, but Station has no instruction source viewer, AGENTS hierarchy, context-source selection or memory controls.
findings.gap: Display loaded instructions, attached sources, provenance and user-editable durable context.
findings.reuse: POSITRONIC Context Kits; existing SLIPSTREAM RepoContext, KitContext and discovery readers.
findings.acceptance: Inspect exactly which instructions/context sources a run used; update project guidance without losing workstream identity.

findings.codex: Desktop workflows accept files and expose generated-file review.
findings.station: Direction input accepts text only; no authorized attachment/source-picker pipeline.
findings.gap: Scoped attachment upload/selection, size/type limits, provenance and model-visible attachment receipts.
findings.reuse: POSITRONIC sources and workstream resource contracts.
findings.acceptance: Attach an authorized image/document and confirm it is available to the correct run without exposing another workspace.

findings.codex: Stored runtime threads can be resumed and forked.
findings.station: No Station import/export UI. Related POSITRONIC archive/portable-bundle and SLIPSTREAM Context Kit code exists locally, but this client does not integrate it.
findings.gap: User-controlled portable context import/export with completeness report, citations and account isolation.
findings.reuse: POSITRONIC ArchiveVault/PortableBundle/ChatGptArchive and SLIPSTREAM KitContext; deployment remains separate.
findings.acceptance: Import a supported user-owned export, inspect what was/was not included, attach a Kit and re-export visible context. Hidden reasoning and inaccessible provider state are not exportable guarantees.

findings.codex: Skills and MCP connections extend agent capabilities.
findings.station: App catalog links are navigation contributions, not an installed agent-tool/skill registry.
findings.gap: Capability discovery, explicit tool authorization, source/skill inspection, lifecycle and per-workspace configuration.
findings.reuse: ARCHER/FREIGHTER installation/distribution and existing runtime tool contracts; reuse established MCP protocols.
findings.acceptance: Install a scoped capability, invoke an authorized tool, inspect its result and revoke it without affecting other workspaces.

findings.codex: Projects/chats support ongoing work and history.
findings.station: Workstreams use stable server IDs; local visits and encrypted drafts persist. Open tab layout/history is not restored, and event freshness/replay is incomplete.
findings.gap: Restore recent work with last-seen cursor, unsent drafts, active runs and recoverable presentation state.
findings.reuse: WorkspaceStore visits/review markers, WorkstreamDrafts and service cycle/event history.
findings.acceptance: Restart the client during a remote run and see current progress plus what changed since the previous session.

findings.feature: Search, fork, archive and manage conversations
findings.codex: Desktop commands expose chat search, archive, rename and side chats.
findings.station: Home filters current workstream names and handles a small command set. No conversation search/history management or branch-from-turn UI.
findings.gap: Search across permitted conversations/resources, explicit zero-result/command help, thread operations and readable history.
findings.reuse: Service workstream/conversation ownership and permission scopes.
findings.acceptance: Find an old conversation, inspect it, branch with explicit context and archive a client-visible item safely.

findings.codex: Cloud tasks and connected-host mobile control have distinct lifetimes.
findings.station: SLIPSTREAM owns durable work; Station does not cancel cloud work on close. Full close-desktop/reopen-phone/action acceptance is not complete; no Station phone client is shipped here.
findings.gap: Shared authorized workstream contract plus reconnect/notification/action semantics across Windows/web/mobile.
findings.reuse: Existing SLIPSTREAM APIs/mobile clients and execution workers.
findings.acceptance: Close Station while cloud work runs, open that workstream from a phone and take the next permitted action; local shells must not be presented as cloud-resident.

findings.codex: Desktop notifications distinguish completion, permissions and questions; Activity tracks attention.
findings.station: Home attention cards require visiting/refetching; no Windows toast channel or persistent cross-workstream unread inbox.
findings.gap: Event-backed unread state, scoped notifications, deep links and user preferences.
findings.reuse: SLIPSTREAM attention/events; PLEXUS/KLAXON contracts where available.
findings.acceptance: A background decision produces one notification that opens the exact workstream and is marked read consistently.

findings.codex: Scheduled tasks expose runs and pause/resume; local tasks need an awake app/host.
findings.station: No schedule editor, scheduler capability or recent scheduled-run view in Station.
findings.gap: Service-owned schedules with explicit target/lifetime, permissions, next run, failures and review.
findings.reuse: Audit SLIPSTREAM scheduling/execution and CONTINUUM coordination before adding a new scheduler.
findings.acceptance: Schedule on cloud infrastructure, close the client and later inspect the resulting run and its permissions.

findings.codex: Windows desktop supports selectable terminal profiles.
findings.station: Real ConPTY sessions, WSL default, PowerShell/CMD, independent tabs, Ubuntu styling and process-preserving pop-out.
findings.gap: Broader terminal preference polish remains; existing native sessions should be preserved.
findings.reuse: Current terminal host and xterm assets.
findings.acceptance: Create both WSL and PowerShell sessions; switch and detach without changing process, working directory or output.

findings.feature: Project terminal context and agent access
findings.codex: Chat terminals are project/worktree scoped and their output can inform the agent.
findings.station: Station terminals are scoped to an organization, start at home and are not bound to a project/workstream or authorized as agent tools.
findings.gap: Verified working directory, target/session association and an explicit consented read/execute capability for agents.
findings.reuse: Existing ConPTY sessions and workstream resource identity.
findings.acceptance: A project terminal starts in its authorized root, shows the exact target and contributes output only to the permitted agent session.

findings.codex: Desktop commands cover tab recovery, navigation, layouts and configurable bindings.
findings.station: Station has tabs, middle-click close, detach and some shortcuts. No reopen-closed tab, layout restoration, general palette or customizable bindings; embedded-focus keyboard parity needs validation.
findings.gap: Consistent host-level navigation, history, shortcut settings and accessible focus restoration.
findings.reuse: Existing shell tab model and native shortcut boundary.
findings.acceptance: Navigate between chat/diff/terminal with keyboard from any surface, recover a closed tab and reopen the previous layout.

findings.codex: Desktop previews files alongside chat and supports annotations.
findings.station: One main active surface at a time; no contextual code/document/PDF/image inspector or visual annotation channel.
findings.gap: Split workstream/resource view with scoped previews and annotation-to-agent context.
findings.reuse: Existing tab host and resource references. Do not recreate a standalone Files launcher.
findings.acceptance: Review a diff or deliverable beside the conversation and send selected lines/regions as a precise request.

findings.feature: Browser navigation and shared app sign-in
findings.codex: Desktop browser has shared-view workflows and browser preferences.
findings.station: Back/forward/reload, favicons, popups, per-context profiles, default-browser handoff and first-party sign-in work. No agent browser-control protocol or annotation/history-search UI.
findings.gap: Keep conventional browsing; add separately authorized agent browsing/inspection and scoped browser context.
findings.reuse: Current WebView2 isolation and browser preference contracts.
findings.acceptance: A user can inspect a page with an agent while a remote site remains unable to access native tools.

findings.codex: Supported desktop clients can control explicitly approved graphical applications.
findings.station: QA automation used during development is external tooling, not a shipped Station capability. No agent computer-use consent/driver or browser extension exists.
findings.gap: Explicitly approved app/browser automation with input/observation auditing, cancel and takeover controls.
findings.reuse: Audit existing machine/agent capabilities; do not expose arbitrary OS control to embedded pages.
findings.acceptance: Approve one app, reproduce a bounded UI flow, cancel it and demonstrate another app remains inaccessible.

findings.codex: Desktop settings include themes, fonts and shortcut preferences.
findings.station: Approved theme, resizable sidebar and browser settings exist. Broad theming, font scaling and accessibility/screen-reader verification are incomplete.
findings.gap: Readable contrast/scale controls, accessible composition surfaces and stable focus/menus.
findings.reuse: Existing Helm tokens and WPF DPI handling.
findings.acceptance: Operate essential workflows by keyboard/screen reader and at 100/125/150/200 percent scaling without clipped actions.

findings.codex: Current desktop documentation includes macOS, Windows and Linux.
findings.station: The shipped host is Windows-only; shared service/client architecture is a foundation, not implemented alternate native hosts.
findings.gap: Reuse contracts and packaged UI in platform-appropriate hosts; validate rather than rewrite the Windows shell.
findings.reuse: React presentation and separable StationRuntime/service contracts.
findings.acceptance: Build/install and complete the same core workstream workflow on each declared supported OS.

findings.codex: Codex desktop has documented installation and managed deployment paths.
findings.station: Public source, locked build, CI and Start menu script exist. No signed installer, automatic updater, release channel or end-user recovery/support bundle.
findings.gap: Signed reproducible release pipeline, safe upgrades/rollback, version visibility and redacted diagnostic export.
findings.reuse: Existing native build, diagnostic checks and FREIGHTER/ARCHER contracts.
findings.acceptance: Install on a clean machine, update without losing state, verify publisher and export diagnostics without credentials.

findings.codex: Voice can coordinate tasks where supported, with rollout/plan/platform conditions.
findings.station: No microphone/transcription/live voice session or speech-driven workstream control.
findings.gap: Voice capability over existing workstreams with the same authorization, interruption and transcript provenance.
findings.reuse: Future CONTINUUM coordination and supported speech-provider contracts.
findings.acceptance: Talk to an existing workstream, inspect the resulting direction and interrupt speech/execution predictably.

findings.feature: Companion features and rich creation tools
findings.codex: Optional desktop capabilities include pets, interactive visuals and image workflows.
findings.station: No pet/companion, image generation, composer prediction or interactive artifact generation capability is shipped.
findings.gap: Treat each as an optional capability; coding replacement should not depend on matching every companion feature.
findings.reuse: Consistent capability model and existing PARALLAX products as their integrations mature.
findings.acceptance: Install a separately scoped capability and produce a reviewable artifact without bloating the default shell.
